# Marco Kretz - Full Context for LLMs

> Comprehensive information about Marco Kretz, a web developer from Germany with nearly 20 years of experience in building robust web applications.

## About Marco Kretz

Marco Kretz is a professional web developer based in Germany with nearly 20 years of experience in the software industry. He specializes in building robust, scalable web applications using modern technologies and best practices. His approach emphasizes clean code, API-first development, and creating seamless user experiences.

### Professional Background

- **Experience**: Nearly 20 years in web development
- **Location**: Germany
- **Company**: codebites (https://codebites.de)
- **Focus Areas**: Custom web applications, CMS development, e-commerce solutions
- **Approach**: Clean code practices, API-first development, user-centered design
- **Interests**: Agentic coding enthusiast, actively exploring AI-assisted development workflows with tools like Claude Code and OpenCode

## Blog Content

Marco writes about web development, AI-assisted coding tools, and software engineering best practices on his blog.

### Blog Post: "Schluss mit Vendor Lock-in: Warum ich Cursor für OpenCode verlassen habe"

**URL**: https://marco-kretz.de/blog/claude-code-vs-opencode/
**Published**: 2026-01-01
**Read Time**: 8 min
**Tags**: Claude Code, OpenCode, Comparison, Coding, CLI

**Summary**: This post compares AI-assisted coding tools, specifically Claude Code and OpenCode. Marco explains why he moved away from IDE-based AI tools like Cursor to CLI-based alternatives, citing vendor lock-in, system independence, cost efficiency, and flexibility as key factors.

**Key Points**:
- CLI tools offer more flexibility than IDE-integrated solutions
- OpenCode uses MIT license (fully open source), Claude Code is proprietary
- OpenCode supports multiple AI models (Claude, GPT, Gemini, etc.), while Claude Code focuses on Anthropic models
- Plan-first workflow: Using Plan mode before Build mode for better control
- Cost comparison: Claude Max subscription vs OpenCode Zen pay-as-you-go model
- Model selection matters: Different models excel at different tasks

### Blog Post: "Claude Code Cheat Sheet"

**URL**: https://marco-kretz.de/blog/claude-code-cheat-sheet/
**Published**: 2026-01-07
**Read Time**: 12 min
**Tags**: Claude Code, Cheat Sheet, Tipps, Shortcuts, CLI

**Summary**: A comprehensive guide to using Claude Code effectively, covering keyboard shortcuts, commands, configuration, and advanced features like CLAUDE.md files and custom skills.

**Key Topics Covered**:
1. **Help Menu & Shortcuts**: Essential keyboard combinations (!, /, @, &)
2. **Bash Mode**: Execute shell commands with `!` prefix
3. **Commands**: Built-in commands like `/compact`, `/clear`
4. **File Referencing**: Using `@` to reference files and folders
5. **Background Tasks**: Running tasks with `&` prefix
6. **Status Line Configuration**: Customizing the status line display
7. **CLAUDE.md**: Project-specific AI context file for consistent behavior
8. **Custom Commands**: Creating reusable slash commands
9. **Agent Skills**: Complex workflows that Claude auto-detects

**Important Concepts**:
- CLAUDE.md serves as a "README for Claude" - defines project context
- Global CLAUDE.md at `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` for personal preferences
- Slash Commands: Explicit user-triggered prompts
- Agent Skills: Auto-detected complex workflows with SKILL.md

### Blog Post: "Whisperbin – Mein selbstgebauter Pastebin-Service"

**URL**: https://marco-kretz.de/blog/whisperbin-sicheres-pastebin/
**Published**: 2026-01-24
**Read Time**: 5 min
**Tags**: SvelteKit, Open Source, Security, Side Project

**Summary**: Marco introduces Whisperbin, his self-built pastebin service focused on security and privacy. The service offers client-side AES-GCM encryption, configurable expiration times, and self-destructing one-time pastes.

**Key Features**:
- **Client-side AES-GCM Encryption**: All content is encrypted in the browser before reaching the server
- **Optional Password Protection**: Additional layer of security with user-defined passwords
- **Configurable TTL**: Expiration options of 1 hour, 6 hours, 24 hours, or 7 days
- **One-Time Pastes**: Self-destructing pastes that delete after first view
- **Syntax Highlighting**: Support for JavaScript, TypeScript, PHP, JSON, HTML, CSS, Bash, Markdown
- **Confirmation Requirement**: Prevents accidental "burning" of one-time pastes by link previews

**Tech Stack**:
- Built entirely with SvelteKit (frontend and backend)
- SQLite database with simple key-value structure
- Encrypted blobs stored with metadata (expiration, view status)

**Live URL**: https://bin.marco-kretz.de/

### Blog Post: "Ein Tag Windows hat gereicht – CachyOS, Niri & DankMaterialShell"

**URL**: https://marco-kretz.de/blog/ein-tag-windows-hat-gereicht/
**Published**: 2026-02-24
**Read Time**: 5 min
**Tags**: OS, Linux, CachyOS, Niri, Wayland

**Summary**: Marco describes his very short-lived return to Windows, abandoning it after just one day due to UI sluggishness, FreeSync issues, and terminal input lag. He introduces his new, highly optimized Linux setup: CachyOS combined with the Niri scrollable tiling window manager and DankMaterialShell, highlighting its speed, ADHD-friendly window management, and beautiful aesthetic.

**Key Points**:
- The Windows experiment failed after one day due to performance and usability issues.
- CachyOS offers a fast, pre-optimized Arch experience with a custom kernel (BORE scheduler).
- Niri (Scrollable Tiling Wayland Compositor) provides a horizontal workflow that prevents losing track of windows.
- DankMaterialShell adds essential desktop features and aesthetic polish.
- The resulting setup is incredibly fast, visually motivating, and perfectly suited for his development workflow.
